issues.description: The solution implementation of Lecture.java declares attribute identifiers using snake_case (e.g. number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all methods reference camelCase attribute names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This mismatch will cause compilation errors and contradicts the attribute names shown in the problem statement UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, etc.), confusing students who inspect the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent with the UML and with the rest of the class. Either rename the declared fields in the solution to camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) or update all usages (constructor and methods) to use the snake_case identifiers. Preferably align with the problem statement and use the camelCase names so template, specification and solution match.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML use camelCase attribute names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution implementation declares the corresponding private fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors). This creates a naming mismatch across artifacts and increases cognitive load for students mapping the requirements to the provided implementation (and may lead to confusion when matching constructor/getter/setter names to the actual fields).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the field identifiers across artifacts. Rename the private fields in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to the camelCase names used in the problem statement: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. Ensure the constructor parameters and all getters/setters reference these exact field names so the problem, template, and solution are consistent.
